To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
data mining methods are suitable to process data from health monitoring systems, but there is a lack of standardization in the data collection, processing and evaluation.

data mining methods for wearable sensors in health monitoring systems can be categorized into three main tasks, namely anomaly detection, prediction, and decision making, and that the data mining methods used for these tasks are mainly supervised and unsupervised learning methods, with the former being more prevalent.

the most common data mining tasks in wearable sensor data analysis are anomaly detection, prediction, and classification; that the most popular methods are based on time series analysis, machine learning, and deep learning; that the data sets used for validation of the methods are often proprietary or not publicly available and that a number of challenges remain for data mining methods applied on health monitoring systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of data from wearable sensors for the purpose of health monitoring.
the use of data mining and machine-learning techniques to process data from wearable sensors for physiological monitoring in health monitoring services.
the development of data mining methods for wearable sensors in health monitoring systems and we have provided an overview of the latest trends in this research field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is still room for improvement and development of data mining methods for wearable sensors in health monitoring systems.
there is a need to consider the data mining tasks and the data mining methods used to process wearable sensor data for health monitoring applications in a holistic way.
the use of wearable sensors for healthcare is a rapidly growing field and the number of data mining and machine leaning methods applied in this area has also increased in the recent years.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the current literature on the topic of data mining for wearable sensors in health monitoring systems has a strong focus on the development and validation of new data mining and machine-learning methods for the analysis of physiological data.
the data sets used for experimental validation have been limited in size.
there has been significant progress in the use of data mining and machine intelligence in the area of health monitoring systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the field of data mining for wearable sensors in healthcare is a growing field with a number of challenges to be solved.
there is a need to develop new methods that are capable of handling large amounts of data, are able to deal with the high variability in the data and that are robust to missing data.
the field of data mining in health monitoring systems is a very active and growing area.
